subsystems.name: Graphene reinforcement
subsystems.role: the carbon sheets that carry load and block dislocation movement inside the metal.
parts: graphene nanoplatelets, graphene oxide, or CVD-grown graphene

subsystems.name: Steel matrix
subsystems.role: the bulk metal that gives ductility, weldability and toughness.
parts: controlled carbon content (extra carbon forms brittle carbides)

subsystems.name: Dispersion stage
subsystems.role: spreads graphene evenly, because clumps act as crack starters.

subsystems.name: Consolidation
subsystems.role: compacts coated powder into fully dense metal.

subsystems.name: Interface control
subsystems.role: manages the carbide layer that forms where graphene meets iron; too much kills ductility.

subsystems.name: Thermomechanical shaping
subsystems.role: turns a billet into plate, bar or structural section.

subsystems.name: Joining and qualification
subsystems.role: makes the material usable in real structures.

buildSteps.title: Produce the graphene
buildSteps.detail: Graphene nanoplatelets are made by liquid-phase exfoliation or reduced graphene oxide, or grown directly on metal powder by chemical vapour deposition. Sheet count and purity must be consistent batch to batch.

buildSteps.title: Coat or mix the powder
buildSteps.detail: Graphene is either grown on the surface of steel powder particles or blended in at roughly 0.1–1% by weight using ball milling or wet mixing with a surfactant to break up agglomerates.

buildSteps.title: Consolidate into a billet
buildSteps.detail: The powder is canned, degassed and densified by hot isostatic pressing or sintering, typically at 1,000–1,200 °C, until porosity is near zero.

buildSteps.title: Control the interface
buildSteps.detail: Heat treatment is tuned so a thin iron-carbide layer bonds graphene to the matrix; too thick and the material turns brittle.

buildSteps.title: Hot work into product
buildSteps.detail: Rolling or forging stretches the billet into plate or section, which tends to align the graphene sheets and raise strength in one direction.

buildSteps.title: Weld and join
buildSteps.detail: Welding melts the matrix locally and destroys the graphene there, so joints must be tested in their own right, not assumed to match the parent metal.

buildSteps.title: Test and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Coupons are tested for tensile strength, fatigue life, fracture toughness and corrosion; a structure needs these properties to be predictable, not just high on average.

buildSteps.title: Certify and scale
buildSteps.detail: The alloy must be written into structural steel codes and produced in tonne quantities at a cost a building project will pay.

prerequisites.why: nanoplatelets are made commercially, but reproducible sheet size, purity and dispersion remain the weak link.

prerequisites.tech: Powder metallurgy and additive manufacturing at scale
prerequisites.why: hot isostatic pressing and laser melting already make dense metal parts, so the shaping route is available.
carbide formation during processing is documented but not yet predictable enough for engineering design.

prerequisites.tech: Structural steel design codes and weld qualification
prerequisites.why: they exist for conventional steels and would need extending to a new alloy class.
powder metallurgy plus graphene is far more expensive per tonne than rolled conventional steel.

pathway.milestone: laboratory coupons of graphene-reinforced metals, chiefly aluminium and copper, show strength gains
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the reinforcement mechanism works in metal matrices.

pathway.milestone: pilot billets of graphene-reinforced steel with tested welded joints
pathway.unlocks: real data on whether joints and toughness survive, which decides whether the material is usable.

pathway.milestone: first commercial parts where weight or wear matters more than price, such as tooling or specialised components
pathway.unlocks: a revenue base that pays for scaling the process.

pathway.milestone: code certification and a demonstration structural member in a tall building
pathway.unlocks: lighter or slimmer columns and floors in very tall or long-span structures, and lower steel mass overall.
